name: TaskView
description: TaskView is a self-hosted project and task management platform for teams. Projects hold task lists, Kanban boards, a dependency graph and sprints, with priorities, tags, deadlines, assignees, recurring tasks and time tracking, plus organizations with role-based permissions, SSO and SCIM, webhooks, GitHub/GitLab/Gitea issue sync, API tokens and an MCP server for AI assistants. This script builds the API and web client from source and runs them with PostgreSQL behind Nginx.

notes.text: The default login user / user1!#Q is publicly documented. Sign in right after the install and claim the account under Account settings > Login and email (set your own login, email and password).

Without SMTP only the default account can sign in: sign-up, invitations and magic-link login all confirm the email address by mail. For more users add the SMTP_* settings from https://taskview.tech/docs/configuration/environment-variables to /opt/taskview_data/.env, consider ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=false (invited emails only), then run systemctl restart taskview.

The API only accepts browser requests from the origins in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and builds email and OAuth links from APP_URL, both set to the container IP in /opt/taskview_data/.env. Change them when the IP changes or TaskView is reached through a hostname or reverse proxy (CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS takes a comma-separated list), then run systemctl restart taskview.

TaskView is source-available, not open source: the TaskView Source-Available License allows personal, family and internal company use, but forbids offering it to third parties as a hosted service or building a competing product on it.

Install and every update build TaskView from source, which needs about 4 GB of RAM (the API bundle is minified with Terser). The running services use far less, so the RAM can be lowered after the install and raised again before an update.
